previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney transplant, type 1 diabetes, and recurrent UTIs was admitted for fevers and myalgias. She had no urinary symptoms, but urinalysis and culture confirmed a complicated UTI due to E. coli resistant to Bactrim and ciprofloxacin. Her creatinine was elevated at 1.3, consistent with pre-renal acute kidney injury from poor oral intake, which resolved with IV fluids. She received IV ceftriaxone and improved clinically. She was transitioned to oral cephalexin for completion of a 14-day course and discharged home. Follow-up with infectious disease was recommended to evaluate restarting suppressive antibiotic therapy. All chronic medications, including immunosuppressants and insulin, were continued without change.
